title: powershell-lsp scan completion receipt, schema version 2
description: Written by scripts/lsp-client.ps1 in scan mode only (dispatch 000304, A2) and validated by scripts/lib/lsp-scan-common.ps1 before a scanned file is reported analyzed. The vocabulary and the structural check live in scripts/lib/lsp-scan-receipt.ps1 (Get-ScanReceiptShapeProblems); tests/PowerShellLsp.ScanReceipt.Tests.ps1 holds this schema and that function together. A receipt that is VALID against this schema certifies nothing on its own: the scanner also re-derives completeness from the receipt's facts and checks the request id, the file, the bytes on disk before and after the analysis and the finding digest. Version 2 (dispatch 000305, B1) lets policy carry the application evidence each party recorded; that evidence is never a certification.

requestId.description: The request id the scanner minted for this file and sent in the hook payload (powershell_lsp_scan.request_id).

file.description: The normalized full path the client analyzed. The scanner requires it to equal the path it asked about.

status.description: One of the four PUBLIC status tokens frozen by CONTRACT.md Tier 1.2. A receipt adds an axis, never a token.

completeness.description: Additive and scan-only. complete: the configured PSScriptAnalyzer pass settled over bytes the scanner can identify. partial: real findings, but that pass did not fully run. failed: nothing about the analysis can be relied on. Only complete is reported analyzed.

pass.description: Which analysis produced the findings: the daemon's PSScriptAnalyzer pass, the client's parser or byte-check short-circuit, or none.

reasons.description: Machine reason codes (Get-ScanReceiptReasonTable). Every reason carries a completeness ceiling; the receipt's completeness is the lowest ceiling among its reasons.

source.description: The identity of the analyzed bytes: SHA-256 (lower-case hex) of the exact bytes the daemon read and handed to PSES (boundary daemon), or that the client read for a short-circuit (boundary client), or none.

daemon.description: What the daemon's scan-mode answer said about the pass it ran, or null when no daemon answered.

engine.description: Engine versions the daemon OBSERVED in the module manifests on disk, or 'unknown'. Never a pinned value standing in for an observation, and never a certification.

config.description: The configuration the daemon was LAUNCHED with, as observed. Unbound: binding the declared scan environment is a later leg (A3).

policy.description: Policy application EVIDENCE (dispatch 000305, B1): unbound when nothing was recorded; observed when the client's adjudication record and, for a PSScriptAnalyzer pass, the daemon's application record ride here. Never verified or certified: only a managed scan (lsp-scan.ps1 -PolicyMode closed) certifies, from this evidence. The vocabulary of the states inside is scripts/lib/lsp-policy.ps1's.

cannotRun.description: The required rules the merged settings file cannot run, by the daemon's static check of that file as read back (dispatch 000307): one 'code: why' string each, the why one of five -- 'no rule of that name' (not a PSScriptAnalyzer built-in rule, and no CustomRulePath that could supply it), 'excluded by '<entry>'' (the ExcludeRules entry that matches it, quoted), 'not in IncludeRules', 'built-in rules not loaded' (a built-in rule beside a CustomRulePath without IncludeDefaultRules = $true) or 'not enabled in Rules' (a configurable built-in rule whose Rules entry under its canonical name does not set Enable = $true; dispatch 000307 correction round 2). Empty when there is none or nothing was merged. Optional: a daemon before dispatch 000307 records none.

validation.description: The daemon's verdict on the settings files the analysis rests on (dispatch 000306): whether PSScriptAnalyzer accepts the repository's and the merged one. They are validated when a PSES session starts, at its first analyzed file, before PSES is handed them; an edit to a settings file during a session is validated at the next session (owner ruling K08), and until then this is the verdict recorded when the session started, while PSES reads the edited file unchecked. Only valid and none let a managed scan certify.

diagnostics.description: The binding over the findings the receipt vouches for: their count, and a SHA-256 over one canonical line per finding (line, col, ruleId, source, severity, message), sorted ordinally.

formatMode.description: The format-on-edit mode the client ran with. A scan child is always 'off'; anything else is formatter-active.

policyResolution.description: A party's own read of the policy: the path it was given, whether it was configured and usable, the fixed reason code when not, and the policy identity (the SHA-256 of the canonical effective policy, ConvertTo-EffectivePolicyText) when usable.
